transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2025-11-03 15:00 PT
Duration: 58 minutes
Attendees: Maya Chen (Redwood AE), Carlos Ortega (Redwood SE), Ravi Patel (Head of ML, Catalyst), Sofia Gomez (Product Lead), Lena Brooks (CTO), Derek Shaw (Procurement)

Auto-summary (auto-gen, may be imperfect): Final pilot readout, majority of success metrics met, economics discussion focused on committed Dedicated pricing vs Hosted pay-as-you-go, security clarifications requested.

[00:00] Maya Chen: All right, hey everyone, thanks for hopping on, appreciate the time. This is Maya — I'll run the readout and Carlos will cover the tuning deep dive.
[00:18] Ravi Patel: Thanks, Maya. Quick note, Lena's on for the first 20, she has to jump to another meeting but wanted to listen to the economic bit.
[00:26] Lena Brooks: Yep, hi all, listening in. Sorry if I cut in.
[00:31] Maya Chen: No worries. High level agenda: results + what we changed, cost model, security/residency Qs, then next steps.
[00:42] Carlos Ortega: Quick callout before we start — logs and the raw CSV from the pilot are attached in the shared Google sheet I linked in the calendar. If you don't have access ping me.
[00:56] Sofia Gomez: Got it, I saw the link.
[01:02] Maya Chen: Okay, benchmark summary first. On the intent classification eval set you gave us (15k utterances), final accuracy was 93% at the threshold you asked for — that's in line with the baseline you provided. The hosted runtime p50 latency averaged ~95ms for 512-token context; p95 at 260ms. Dedicated config dropped that to p50 ~48ms and p95 ~120ms under the pilot workload. Error rates were below 1.1% for both.
[01:34] Ravi Patel: Those Dedicated numbers look great. What's the input batch size during Dedicated runs?
[01:40] Carlos Ortega: We used continuous batching with target batch 8 and a soft limit at 16 for the Dedicated tests; that was tuned during weeks 2-3 to hit the p50 target without spiking p95. We also enabled prefix KV caching for the top 20% of repeated conversation prefixes — that knocked per-token compute by approximately 18% in hotspots.
[02:05] Sofia Gomez: Quick question on the accuracy: the 93% — is that before or after the post-processing reranker?
[02:12] Carlos Ortega: That's after the reranker thresholding you requested. Raw model top-1 was about 91.2% on your set. The reranker and simple rule-based tie-breaks pushed it to 93.
[02:24] Ravi Patel: Gotcha. Can you repeat the cost delta — Dedicated vs Hosted — at our expected QPS? We modeled 25 qps sustained and 75 burst.
[02:33] Maya Chen: Sure — in the deck you'll get the exact token-level math but high-level: Hosted pay-as-you-go at the pilot volume projects to about 3.7x the per-request cost of the equivalent Dedicated reserved capacity when you amortize monthly commit over your 25 qps baseline. But Dedicated requires a 3- or 12-month commit to realize those numbers. If you only need bursty spikes and no commit, Hosted is more flexible albeit pricier.
[02:59] Derek Shaw: On the procurement side, our finance team won't entertain a 12-month lock without a clear business case. Does Redwood support quarterly commitments or a hybrid?
[03:09] Maya Chen: We do have 3-month reserved options for Dedicated in some regions and a hybrid model where you keep a smaller Dedicated footprint plus burstable Hosted capacity for occasional spikes. We can model that in the deck.
[03:21] Lena Brooks: Security — your SOC2 and ISO attestations? Also, how does logging work for PII? We need clear retention/rotation and KMS integration detail.
[03:31] Carlos Ortega: We provided the SOC2 Type II report in the security packet last week; for the private deployments we support KMS/HSM integrations and can map logs to customer-owned storage in a VPC. For Hosted, we support configurable retention windows and redaction rules — but we recommend the Private control plane + VPC if you need strict residue data separation.
[03:51] Ravi Patel: Is there an option for partial redaction at inference time? Like mask inputs containing account numbers before storing?
[03:58] Carlos Ortega: Yes, we have pre-ingest hooks and a lightweight lambda-based scrub that can run in your VPC to redact. We also have token-level auditing if you want full traceability with encrypted logs.
[04:12] Sofia Gomez: About data residency, some EU customers require data never leave region. Does Redwood support region-restricted hosting?
[04:19] Maya Chen: Yes, we have regional deployments; for production you can pin to a region. For the pilot we were in the US-west region per your earlier ask but we can model EU region pricing and latency if that's needed.
[04:31] Ravi Patel: Back to performance — Carlos, during week 3 you changed the quantization profile. Any loss in accuracy?
[04:37] Carlos Ortega: We moved from 8-bit dynamic to a mixed-precision Q4 profile for the inference path. Measured delta on your eval set was -0.3% absolute on top-1 before reranker, so negligible when combined with the reranker. The cost savings there were meaningful — about 12% CPU/GPU compute reduction.
[04:58] Maya Chen: Also worth calling out: we tried a more aggressive KV cache eviction during the midday spike and that reduced memory pressure but raised p95 by roughly 10ms — tradeoff worth noting if you prioritize tight p95 SLOs.
[05:13] Ravi Patel: Can you remind me of the failure behavior — if Dedicated nodes are temporarily unavailable, do we failover to Hosted? How seamless is that?
[05:21] Carlos Ortega: We can configure multi-tier routing: primary Dedicated pool with automatic fallback to Hosted or a smaller Dedicated spare pool. There is a cold-start delta during fallback — usually a 200-600ms spike depending on model size — but we can smooth that with warm standby if you want guaranteed latency.
[05:39] Derek Shaw: If we go Dedicated, any early termination penalties? We need clarity for legal.
[05:45] Maya Chen: Contract specifics vary, but standard Dedicated contracts have step-downs and an early termination schedule. We'll share the contract template so your procurement can see the exact clauses.
[05:53] Lena Brooks: From an exec perspective, I need the business case: what's the ROI timeline if we commit to Dedicated vs staying Hosted for 12 months?
[06:01] Maya Chen: In the slide deck I'll include a 12- and 24-month model. At your 25 qps baseline, Dedicated crosses even with Hosted around month 6-8 depending on burst profile. The savings accelerate with usage increases.
[06:14] Ravi Patel: Any notable competitor differences? I know we also ran small tests on Anthropic; we want to make sure latency and cost comparisons are fair.
[06:22] Carlos Ortega: We included side-by-side in the Appendix: we normalized for batch size and sequence length, but some competitors trade latency for quality differently. We can walk that appendix in the exec readout.
[06:34] Sofia Gomez: For the exec readout, we want a one-pager for the CFO that highlights savings and risk summary. Can you do that?
[06:41] Maya Chen: Absolutely, one-pager with topline numbers and a couple of caveats — we'll get that in the packet.
[06:48] Lena Brooks: Quick question on observability — can we get token-level cost attribution per route? I want to show product owners exact $ per feature.
[06:57] Carlos Ortega: Yes, Console has token-level breakdown per route; we also export daily CSVs for your internal chargeback. That was enabled in the pilot logs you received.
[07:08] Ravi Patel: Anything surprising in the logs?
[07:11] Carlos Ortega: There was a small batch of long-tail prompts that triggered memory churn — we flagged those in the anomaly sheet. We recommended pre-filtering or limiting max tokens for those routes to avoid sporadic p95 spikes.
[07:25] Derek Shaw: On procurement timeline — assuming we sign off next week, what's realistic for go-live on Dedicated?
[07:32] Maya Chen: If contracts move quickly and you approve the commit, provisioning Dedicated in-region takes 2-3 weeks including network setup. Private deployment will add more time for VPC peering and KMS setup — typically 4-6 weeks.
[07:45] Lena Brooks: Okay that timeline works. I'll need the one pager and the cost model by Friday.
[07:51] Maya Chen: We'll aim for that. Carlos, anything else on tuning?
[07:55] Carlos Ortega: Just to summarize the tuning knobs we touched: continuous batching targets, prefix KV cache for repeated prompts, mixed-precision quant profile, and the eviction policy we adjusted. I can send a short runbook with the exact flags and config snippets.
[08:11] Ravi Patel: Yes please send the runbook. Also can you include the exact evaluation script we used so we can re-run in-house?
[08:18] Carlos Ortega: Yep, I'll include the script and the docker image tag we used.
[08:22] Sofia Gomez: On next steps, let's recap — Deloitte... sorry — Derek, could you confirm procurement constraints?
[08:29] Derek Shaw: Sure. Primary constraints: no > 12-month financial lock without explicit board approval, prefer quarterly review points, legal needs to see indemnity and data processing addendum. I'll share preferred contract language by Monday.
[08:42] Maya Chen: Great — to close we'll send: final consolidated deck + one-pager, cost model, raw logs, runbook, and contract template. Also propose 30m exec readout for next Thursday 
[08:58] Lena Brooks: That works for me.
[09:01] Ravi Patel: Works for me too.
[09:03] Maya Chen: Any final questions?
[09:05] Sofia Gomez: None from me.
[09:07] Derek Shaw: All good.
[09:09] Maya Chen: Okay thanks everyone. We'll follow up with the materials and proposed time for the exec readout.
[09:16] (meeting ends)

Notes: transcription contains minor audio artifacts and speaker overlap. References: deck link (shared via calendar), pilot logs (Google sheet), appendix with competitor normalization (attached in drive).
